summary.text: A 14-year-old male competitive swimmer with a mild pollen allergy and no medications or notable history had occasional mild morning chest discomfort for six months, then acute sharp anterior chest pain. Vital signs and examination were unremarkable; CT showed a small amount of mediastinal emphysema, and he was admitted for observation and pain control with resolution of pain and discharge on the third hospital day.

Physical activity resumed two weeks later and full activity was reached one month after initiating exercise. Four months later he developed recurrent chest pain during underwater training, considered a probable recurrence, with a normal chest radiograph, deferred repeat CT, conservative management and discharge on the second hospital day.

About three months later a third episode of throat pain extending to the epigastrium was confirmed on chest CT as left-sided mediastinal emphysema, with rehospitalization for four days. Activity was restricted for two months with supervised stretching and diaphragmatic breathing, followed by resistance training and gradual return to swimming; rehabilitation was completed over three months and he remained free of recurrent SPM.
